chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The ritual bath (ghusl) is [required] from the sexual impurity (janabah), and on the day of Friday, and on the two Eids, and when you enter the state of Ihram, and when you enter Makkah and Al-Madinah, and on the day of 'Arafah, and on the day you perform Ziyarah of the House, and when you enter the Ka'bah, and during the night of the nineteenth, twenty-first, and twenty-third of the month of Ramadan, and [for] the one who washes a deceased person.
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the comprehensive list of occasions requiring ghusl in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between obligatory acts like janabah and recommended acts such as entering Makkah and Al-Madinah. It highlights the spiritual purification associated with key moments in the lunar calendar, including the specific nights of the 19th, 21st, and 23rd of Ramadan, reflecting the tradition's emphasis on ritual purity during worship and pilgrimage.
